hypothesis: Branches carrying greater U->D than D->U orientation transition probability align with a predeclared composite present-day environmental shift toward higher BIO15 and lower BIO1.

interpretation.supported: The predeclared composite (+BIO15, -BIO1) transition-regime direction is positive on all six accepted topologies and unusually strong relative to all count-preserving state maps in the n>=5 primary hypothesis panel.
interpretation.axis_decomposition: BIO15 alone is not exceptional in n>=5, whereas the lower-BIO1 component is. The supported object is therefore the composite transition-regime hypothesis, with stronger contribution from the lower-temperature component, not a unique precipitation-seasonality driver.
interpretation.causal_boundary: This is repeated phylogenetic transition-regime concordance using present-day taxon niche centroids. It does not establish transition-time climatic causation, selection, adaptation, or a physiological mediator.

claim_ceiling: Do not call BIO1 or BIO15 a causal driver.
Do not call the exact state-map fraction a P value from biological replicates; it is an exhaustive finite-map null rank.
Present-day taxon centroids are not historical transition-time environments.
Do not claim adaptation, selection, independent origins, or transition-time fitness.
